asked: Why do the announced results for Obio/Akpor differ from the result sheets on the portal?
found: The announced Obio/Akpor figures were 80,239 for APC, 3,829 for LP, 368 for PDP and 161 for NNPP. Leadership and NewsOnline reported these numbers.

Several outlets added up the polling unit sheets on INEC's portal (IReV) and said the sums did not match the announcement. The BBC counted far fewer APC votes and far more LP votes from the sheets than were announced. NewsOnline, which carried a Premium Times report, reached the same kind of gap. Both said sheets that were blurred, missing or not yet uploaded could only add votes, so they would not explain the LP drop.

Earlier, CDD's fact-check looked at a tweet that claimed a mismatch. CDD said many Obio/Akpor sheets were not visible or were uploaded badly. It said nobody could reliably add up the portal figures, and it rated the tweet's specific numbers unverifiable. This is a caution about any total, including ones from this count.

Reporters also found problems on some sheets themselves. NewsOnline and a CCIJ investigation, published on TheCable, described figures overwritten or whited out, and digits that did not match the words written beside them. They also reported some sheets from the wrong election. The BBC said INEC's Port Harcourt spokesperson blamed time and staff shortages for some collation problems. INEC's headquarters would not comment because of court cases, and Leadership reported INEC called the Premium Times report prejudicial for the same reason.
questions: Which sheets or collation records explain the gap between the announced figures and the portal sheets? The reporting does not settle this.
Did the overwritten sheets reflect changes made at the polling unit, or were they altered later? The reporting describes them but does not say.
Has any court or INEC review given a final finding on the Obio/Akpor figures? The sources I read do not say.

asked: Why do the announced results for Oyigbo differ from the result sheets on the portal?
found: The BBC looked at this in a May 2023 investigation. It added up the result sheets that INEC put online for Rivers State. It named Oyigbo as one of two areas with the biggest gaps between those sheets and the announced result.

The BBC also found a signed collation sheet for Oyigbo, photographed and shared on social media. It says the figures on that sheet closely matched its own sheet-by-sheet count for the two leading parties.

The BBC says an official named Dr Dickson Ariaga read out the Oyigbo result at the state declaration on 27 February. It says he read the smaller parties' figures as they were on the collation sheet. For APC, it says he read 16,630 where the sheet showed 2,731. For LP, it says he read 10,784 where the sheet showed 22,289. These announced figures are the same ones in your question.

The BBC also reports that the Federal College of Education in Omoku, where he said he worked, told it that it had no record of anyone by that name. An INEC spokesman in Port Harcourt said that, because of a shortage of time and staff, some people had been taken on without their identity documents being checked. He said that if the man had misdescribed himself, he was dishonest. INEC headquarters told the BBC it could not comment because of court cases. Dr Ariaga did not respond to the BBC.

On sheets that are missing or unreadable, the BBC says they would have added votes to each party's total, not taken them away. That is why it says they cannot explain LP's lower announced figure. Separately, Yiaga Africa said in March 2023 that the Rivers state results were inconsistent with its own sample-based estimates. It asked INEC to explain. The Yiaga statement I read does not mention Oyigbo.

asked: Is it true that INEC's results portal was hacked during the 2023 presidential election?
found: No public report shows that INEC's results portal (IReV) was hacked during the 2023 presidential election. INEC says it was not. Its spokesperson told Africa Check that neither the INEC website nor the portal was hacked "before, during or after" the election. On 26 Feb 2023, INEC also said the upload problems were "not due to any intrusion or sabotage".

On election morning, an influencer claimed the portal had been breached. The BBC checked the claim. It found the site shown was a phishing site pretending to be INEC's. Later, a viral Facebook post said a "Russian hacker" had released the real results. Africa Check found no evidence for this. The photo was of a Russian student from 2017.

Uploads of presidential results did fail on election day. In a report released on 23 Feb 2024, INEC said this was a configuration error. It said the presidential race was a nationwide contest, not tied to any state, so the system could not store the uploads. INEC said it fixed this with software updates. The first presidential result sheet went up at 8:55pm. Heavy traffic and switched-off devices caused further delays. INEC also said it added security checks because of the real threat of cyberattacks.

Some people have made other claims. An APC campaign official said on TV that opposition parties brought in hackers, but that none succeeded. This was an assertion from an official, with no evidence given. Former INEC chairman Attahiru Jega said in Jan 2024 that he believed some politicians "may have infiltrated" the portal. Opposition parties said INEC either colluded or its system was down. Separately, the communications minister said there were about 13 million attacks on government websites on election day. A Galaxy Backbone attack figure was reported, then disowned by the company. None of these said the portal was successfully hacked.

Ní òwúrọ̀ ọjọ́ ìdìbò, ònítàn-ọ̀rọ̀ kan (influencer) sọ pé wọ́n ti wọ inú ìkànnì àbájáde náà. BBC ṣàyẹ̀wò ẹ̀sùn yìí. Ó rí i pé ojú-òpó tí wọ́n fihàn jẹ́ ojú-òpó ẹ̀tàn (phishing) tó ń díbọ́n bí ti INEC. Lẹ́yìn náà, àkọsílẹ̀ kan tó gbilẹ̀ lórí Facebook sọ pé "ọ̀daràn orí ayélujára ọmọ ilẹ̀ Rọ́ṣíà" ti tú àbájáde òtítọ́ jáde. Africa Check kò rí ẹ̀rí kankan fún èyí. Fọ́tò náà jẹ́ ti akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ ọmọ ilẹ̀ Rọ́ṣíà kan ní ọdún 2017.

Ìgbésókè àbájáde ìdìbò ààrẹ kò yọrí ní ọjọ́ ìdìbò. Nínú ìròyìn kan tí INEC tẹ̀ jáde ní ọjọ́ 23 Oṣù Kejì ọdún 2024, INEC sọ pé àṣìṣe ìṣètò (configuration) ni ó fà á. Ó sọ pé ìdíje ààrẹ jẹ́ ìdíje jákèjádò orílẹ̀-èdè, kò so mọ́ ìpínlẹ̀ kankan, nítorí náà ẹ̀rọ náà kò lè tọ́jú àwọn ohun tí wọ́n gbé sókè. INEC sọ pé òun ti tún èyí ṣe pẹ̀lú àtúnṣe sọ́fítíwẹ́ẹ̀. Fọ́ọ̀mù àbájáde ìdìbò ààrẹ àkọ́kọ́ lọ sókè ní aago mẹ́jọ àti ìṣẹ́jú márùn-dín-nígba (8:55pm) alẹ́. Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ èrò lórí ayélujára àti àwọn ẹ̀rọ tí wọ́n pa fa ìdádúró síwájú sí i. INEC tún sọ pé òun fi àwọn àyẹ̀wò ààbò kún un nítorí ewu gidi ti ìkọlù orí ayélujára.

Àwọn kan ti sọ àwọn ohun mìíràn. Òṣìṣẹ́ ìpolongo APC kan sọ lórí tẹlifíṣọ̀n pé àwọn ẹgbẹ́ alátakò mú àwọn adigunjalè orí ayélujára wá, ṣùgbọ́n ẹnikẹ́ni kò yege. Èyí jẹ́ àfẹnusọ láti ọ̀dọ̀ òṣìṣẹ́ kan, láìsí ẹ̀rí tí wọ́n fi lélẹ̀. Ọ̀gá àgbà INEC tẹ́lẹ̀ rí, Attahiru Jega, sọ ní Oṣù Kínní ọdún 2024 pé òun gbàgbọ́ pé àwọn òṣèlú kan "lè ti wọ inú" ìkànnì náà. Àwọn ẹgbẹ́ alátakò sọ pé yálà INEC dìtẹ̀ mọ́ wọn ni, tàbí ẹ̀rọ rẹ̀ ti bàjẹ́. Lọ́tọ̀, mínísítà ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ sọ pé nǹkan bí mílíọ̀nù mẹ́tàlá (13 million) ìkọlù ló wáyé lórí àwọn ojú-òpó wẹ́ẹ̀bù ìjọba ní ọjọ́ ìdìbò. Wọ́n ròyìn iye ìkọlù kan lòdì sí Galaxy Backbone, lẹ́yìn náà ilé-iṣẹ́ náà sẹ́ ẹ. Kò sí èyíkéyìí nínú wọn tó sọ pé wọ́n gbọ́ ìkànnì àbájáde náà ní àgbẹ́yọ.

asked: I heard INEC will not publish ward collation results for the 2027 election. Is that true?
found: Partly true, but the wording matters. On 17 November 2026, INEC's ICT Director, Lawrence Bayode, said INEC cannot put ward, local government and state collation results on its online portal (IReV) for the 2027 elections. He said: "We have not built the system; we have not tested the system." Premium Times reported this from a Yiaga Africa roundtable in Abuja.

This is about publishing results online. The reports do not say INEC will keep these results secret. IReV currently shows only polling unit results (Form EC8A). Ward, local government and state results are on Forms EC8B, EC8C and EC8D, and those forms would not be on the portal.

The Electoral Act 2026 has a rule on copies of these forms. As summarised by The Sun, Section 71 says copies of completed result forms at ward, local government, state and national levels must be given to polling agents and police officers where available. Section 62 lets any person or party get certified copies from INEC's result register for a fee. I did not read the Act itself.

Reactions have followed. Yiaga Africa had earlier asked INEC to upload ward and local government results (The Guardian, July 2026). The ADC presidential campaign council said the decision was unacceptable and asked for publication at every collation level (Prime Times, 19 November 2026).
questions: Will INEC give ward, local government and state result forms to the public in some other way, such as a website or printed copies?
Will INEC change its position before the election, given the calls from Yiaga Africa and the ADC?
How much of the Section 71 rule on copies of result forms will voters, as opposed to party agents, be able to use in practice?

asked: Na ji cewa INEC ba za ta wallafa sakamakon tattara kuri'u na mazaba (ward) na zaben 2027 ba. Shin gaskiya ne?
found: Gaskiya ne a wani bangare, amma kalmomin da aka yi amfani da su suna da muhimmanci. A ranar 17 ga Nuwamba, 2026, Daraktan ICT na INEC, Lawrence Bayode, ya ce INEC ba za ta iya sanya sakamakon tattara kuri'u na mazaba, na ƙaramar hukuma da na jiha a shafinta na intanet (IReV) ba a zabukan 2027. Ya ce: "Ba mu gina tsarin ba; ba mu gwada tsarin ba." Premium Times ne ya ruwaito wannan daga wani taron tattaunawa na Yiaga Africa a Abuja.

Wannan yana game da wallafa sakamako ne a intanet. Rahotannin ba su ce INEC za ta ɓoye waɗannan sakamakon ba. A yanzu IReV yana nuna sakamakon rumfunan zabe (polling unit) kawai (Form EC8A). Sakamakon mazaba, na ƙaramar hukuma da na jiha suna cikin fom din EC8B, EC8C da EC8D, kuma waɗannan fom din ba za su kasance a shafin ba.

Dokar Zabe ta 2026 tana da ka'ida kan kwafin waɗannan fom. Kamar yadda The Sun ya taƙaita, Sashe na 71 ya ce dole a ba wa wakilan jam'iyyu a rumfunan zabe da jami'an 'yan sanda, inda suke, kwafin fom din sakamako da aka cike a matakin mazaba, ƙaramar hukuma, jiha da ƙasa. Sashe na 62 yana bai wa kowane mutum ko jam'iyya damar samun kwafi da aka tabbatar daga rajistar sakamako ta INEC a kan biyan kuɗi. Ban karanta Dokar da kanta ba.

An fara mayar da martani. Yiaga Africa ta riga ta nemi INEC ta ɗora sakamakon mazaba da na ƙaramar hukuma (The Guardian, Yuli 2026). Majalisar yakin neman zaben shugaban ƙasa na ADC ta ce wannan shawara ba abar karɓa ba ce, kuma ta nemi a wallafa sakamako a kowane matakin tattara kuri'u (Prime Times, 19 ga Nuwamba, 2026).
